oneLine: Receives deliveries at the dock: from an announced ASN to a closed, counted receipt.

rows.title: Announce a delivery
rows.story: A supplier announces what is coming. The ASN is only accepted if every SKU on it is a product the warehouse knows.

then.does: feeds its ASN view so a door can be planned

rows.title: Cancel an announcement
rows.story: The supplier withdraws the announcement. It only works while nothing has been received yet.

then.does: cancels a booking when all its ASNs are cancelled

rows.title: Keep the appointments copy
rows.story: The dock booking lives in dock-scheduling. Here a read-only copy follows its bookings, reschedules and door changes, so receiving never has to ask.
rows.policy: Whenever an inbound appointment is booked, cancelled or moved, update the local copy

rows.title: Keep the product list
rows.story: Every product that product-master registers becomes a known SKU, so an ASN can be checked without a live call.
rows.policy: Whenever a product is registered, add its SKU to the known SKUs

rows.title: Keep the dock-door list
rows.story: Only inbound dock doors matter here. facility-layout announces every location slot; receiving keeps the doors it can use.
rows.policy: Whenever a slot is registered, keep it only if it is an inbound dock door

rows.title: Open a receipt at the door
rows.story: The truck is at the door. Dock staff open a receipt for the ASN, with or without an appointment, and the ASN moves to Receiving.

rows.title: Count a line
rows.story: Dock staff count what is on the pallet and record it as Good or Damaged. Only Good units become stock.

then.does: books the Good units as staged stock

rows.title: Receive by scan
rows.story: Dock staff scan a carton label. An accepted carton books its contents; a refused scan is not an error, it becomes a recorded finding.

then.does: creates or links the carton's container
keeps a copy of the carton and the finding

rows.title: Close the receipt
rows.story: Dock staff close the receipt. It reports every difference against the ASN, flags cartons that never showed up and sends the receiving advice.

then.does: keeps a copy of the closed receipt

rows.title: Complete the ASN
rows.story: When the receipt closes, the ASN closes with it, in the same transaction. Nobody has to remember to do it.
rows.policy: Whenever a receipt closes, close its ASN in the same transaction

rows.title: Measure dock-to-stock: the gate
rows.story: The yard reports when the truck reached the gate. That is the start of the dock-to-stock clock.
rows.policy: Whenever a visit checks in, store the arrival and check whether the evidence is complete

rows.title: Measure dock-to-stock: the shelf
rows.story: inventory-storage reports when a carton was stowed. When the last Good carton is on the shelf, the dock-to-stock time is known.
rows.policy: Whenever a container is stowed, store the stow and check whether the evidence is complete

rows.title: Chase a late advice
rows.story: A periodic sweep looks for open receipts whose receiving advice is past its deadline and raises an overdue notice.
rows.policy: Every sweep, any open receipt past its advice deadline raises an overdue notice

hotspots.text: No tolerance policy: every over-receipt is reported, never silently accepted. A tolerance is a later decision.
Damaged units are counted but have no quarantine flow. They are not booked as stock.
If inventory-storage rejects a line, it skips and logs. The receipt stays the source of truth, nothing compensates.
The deprecated appointment routes stay in the API pending a decision, although dock-scheduling owns appointments.

opportunities.text: The receiving advice has no reader yet. Partner connectivity could send it back to the supplier.
